technical_and_design_decisions: The NIO stack toggle will be implemented as a boolean flag in deploy.properties that conditionally activates the NIO-based connectors without restarting the runtime.
WebSocket components will be implemented as a pair of new Mule components (websocket:inbound-endpoint and websocket:outbound-endpoint) leveraging the standard Java EE WebSocket API.

Registry pairing will be done via an out-of-band HTTPS REST call from the ESB instance to the Registry using a shared API key; a lightweight heartbeat/license-check client will run as a background agent.
HTTP endpoint registration with the paired Registry will be performed at application deployment time by enumerating the HTTP inbound endpoints of each deployed app and POSTing them to the Registry.
The Dynamic Lookup component will resolve endpoint URIs at runtime by querying the Registry over a cached REST client; results will be cached with a configurable TTL to avoid hot-path latency.
Throttling policies will be expressed as JSON descriptors downloaded from the Registry and enforced by a new policy interceptor placed in the Mule inbound pipeline.

Custom business events and transaction IDs will be exposed via a MVEL/OGNL expression evaluated on each event, with results appended to a dedicated log appender (SLF4J with MDC) so existing log patterns can include them.
MVEL 2.1.8 will replace the previous version as a transitive dependency; DataMapper and any direct MVEL evaluators will be smoke-tested for breaking API changes.

JDBC support for the five remaining databases will be provided as packaged default connection templates (driver class, sample URL, and JPA/JDBC-compatible config snippets) shipped in the distribution.
Query debug logging for JDBC will hook the underlying DataSource's statement-execution path (or use a logging JDBC wrapper) and emit SQL via the existing org.mule logger at DEBUG level.
assumptions: The developer is experienced with the Mule 3.x codebase, Spring, and the Mule transport/component model.
All 8 user stories are developed in a single increment; cross-feature regression testing is required.
Detailed specs linked from U2 and U3 (corp wiki pages) are unavailable, so a reasonable, self-contained interpretation of the requirements is used.
A single developer performs all the work; effort is measured in work-hours (not elapsed time).
No third-party procurement or lengthy procurement/legal review is required for the MVEL upgrade or new JDBC drivers.
Unit tests and integration tests are included in the per-activity estimates; dedicated end-to-end system testing is broken out as its own activity.
The NIO stack and the legacy IO stack can coexist, so the toggle is purely configuration and does not require rewriting transports.
Throttling enforcement happens at the Mule inbound layer; no modifications to back-end services are required.
Documentation updates for new properties, components, and DB templates are scoped as a single activity rather than per feature.
No new build infrastructure, CI pipeline changes, or release-engineering work is included.
